purpose: Physical-vehicle data collection plan. The runs below are executed and uploaded as raw outputs; metrics, figures and conclusions are produced from them on the receiving side.
collector_responsibilities: measure the track and the start/stop poses
upload raw outputs with a filled handover.json

supports: one operator-accepted two-lap physical execution without contact
no reverse on the second lap of that run
onboard pipeline timing and resource cost
internal consistency of reference, command and onboard estimate
does_not_support: absolute trajectory or speed accuracy (no external reference)
success rate or repeatability (one accepted run per condition)
isolated contribution of any component (no hardware ablation)
longitudinal plant convergence (12 of 20 updates, confidence 0.0, inverse never applied)
generalization (single track, used to tune the controller)
end-to-end actuation latency distribution (no per-command PWM trace)

sessions.varies: nothing; fresh state each run, battery condition logged

sessions.purpose: Controller A/B against the retained profile
sessions.varies: profile only; alternate order with S1 run by run
unlocks: the one controlled comparison available without new code

sessions.purpose: A layout the controller was never tuned on
sessions.varies: track layout, rearranged once before the session and measured

sessions.purpose: Longest straight that fits the room
sessions.varies: track layout maximizing straight length, measured like any other layout
unlocks: more valid longitudinal identifier updates, so the online identification claim can be decided

sessions.purpose: Stationary reference with the car parked and never armed
sessions.varies: nothing; the car must not move or be touched
unlocks: stationary false-motion measurement against a known zero

sessions.purpose: Hand-driven capture with varied motion, for the estimator evaluation on real data
sessions.command: Pi: tools/core/apex_manual_control_up.sh (estimator and raw logging on, autonomous planners off); PC: real_vehicle/tools/pc/run_windows_gamepad_ros_bridge_pc.sh
sessions.command_status: not exercised recently; verify bring-up before recording and report instead of modifying the scripts if it fails
sessions.varies: nothing in the setup; the variety is in the driving
must_contain: one pass along the longest available straight at roughly constant speed
at least one left and one right turn
a return to the start marks with the final pose measured
unlocks: RPE at fixed horizons and segment drift on real data
the real-data counterpart of the simulated odometry comparison
constraints: entirely inside the camera field of view
driven slowly by hand, no mission, no autonomy
sessions.note: highest-value optional session for the odometry contribution

blocked_without_new_code.note: These need a runtime switch that does not exist today and are not part of the collection scope. They are evaluated in simulation and by offline replay of the recorded raw sensor data. Do not emulate them by editing start_apex_pipeline.sh or the YAML.
handled_by: simulation campaign on the reconstructed layouts
offline replay of the uploaded raw scans and IMU

track_reference.verdict: Measured pole lengths plus photos are sufficient for a metric ground-truth map (scale error, loop-closure error, true mean speed from path length over lap time). Per-timestamp accuracy (ATE/RPE) additionally requires one immobile camera; the known pole positions serve as its calibration target. Expected reference budget with 1080p covering the whole track: 1-3 cm.
tier_a_required: length of every pole/segment in metres, tape-measured to +/- 0.01 m
hand sketch of the layout with lengths and lane width
pole height above the floor, cross-section shape and width/diameter, material or surface finish, and whether all poles are identical
4+ photos from different corners plus the highest viewpoint available
a tape measure or known-length object visible in at least one photo
floor surface type and anything that moved during the session
tier_b_required: tripod-mounted phone, immobile, no zoom, whole track in frame, 1080p/30fps minimum, one file per run
>= 6 known floor points visible in every frame
flat high-contrast marker on the car roof (ArUco or black cross on white A5)
measured marker height above floor and marker offset from the LiDAR centre
camera position and height relative to one identified pole corner, +/- 0.05 m
time sync: film a screen running 'date -Ins' for ~5 s with the camera already recording, and note each run's wall-clock launch time
track_reference.insufficient_alone: a still photo carries no information about where the car was at a given instant
used_for: metric ground-truth map for the physical runs
calibration target for the fixed-camera trajectory reference
rebuilding each layout in the simulator so simulated and physical runs are compared on the same geometry
track_reference.why_pole_geometry: height, cross-section and material determine what the LiDAR returns, so a layout that cannot be reconstructed from the upload cannot be compared against simulation

git_notes: *.csv is ignored repository-wide: stage run directories with 'git add -f'
video stays out of git (100 MB per-file limit): share a link and record each file's sha256 in handover.json
nothing is deleted from the Pi until the upload is confirmed
pull_request_must_state: attempts vs completions with stop reasons
any deviation from the frozen configuration

hard_rules: retain every attempt, including failures and operator stops
never weaken a confidence gate, clearance limit, speed cap or recovery behaviour to obtain a cleaner run
never retrain or replace the weights; the listed hashes must keep matching
do not rearrange the track mid-session except where S3 and S4 require it, and then only before that session's first run
onboard map and estimated trajectory are onboard estimates, not ground truth
physical_runs_role: The physical runs validate transfer; the controlled comparisons and ablations live in simulation, where ground truth is available. S6 supplies the real sequences needed to compute the same open-loop estimator metrics on hardware.
